name: Lacustrine-Seif
description: The sea here is thick with dissolved metals, so sunsets burn green and gold above the waves. Beneath them wait a subterranean ocean, and everything the light never reaches.
The air carries burnt sugar and sulfur, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
The oldest impact basin predates the system's estimated age by a comfortable margin. The survey bureau has quietly stopped publishing the numbers.
Mining charters include clauses about 'subsurface events' that lawyers refuse to define.
